children: New Delhi, Nov. 8 -- Diwali Muhurat trading session: Shares of Safe Enterprises Retail Fixtures Limited opened sharply lower during the special trading session on Sunday, November 8. The steep decline in the NSE SME stock stood in stark contrast to the positive opening of the benchmark Nifty 50 and Sensex.
Safe Enterprises Retail Fixtures shares were trading nearly 9% lower during Sunday's special session as investors reacted to the company's quarterly results announced after market hours on Friday.

The sharp decline in Safe Enterprises Retail Fixtures came after the company reported a 34.57% decline in its net profit after tax (PAT) to Rs.21.75 crore in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27. Its net profit stood at Rs.33.24 crore in the year ago period.

Its revenue from operations decreased to Rs.77.87 crore in Q2FY27 against Rs.112.37 crore reported in the year ago period. Its net operating EBITDA stood at Rs.2,564.36 lakh in H1FY27, 39% decline from Rs.4,232.80 lakh against H1FY26.

The stock was trading 5.89% lower at Rs.216.30 per share on NSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.1,002.00 crore at 2:50 pm. The NSE SME stock had declined more than 9% earlier today to dip to an intraday low of Rs.200 per share. The stock has declined 14% in one month, 17.29% in 2026 so far, but has surged 8.07% in one year.
